published_source: Table 8 column 3, Marketing Science 37(1) (papers/mksc/mksc.2017.1051.pdf, read Nov 2): bins short_0_1 0.47 (0.057); medium_2_24 0.26 (0.058). published_coef = equal-weight mean of the 2 printed bins (Hull's post summary over event_structure.post_summary); no SE of the mean is printed. The printed values agree with authors_code (exact re-run) to printed precision.

authors_code.source: replication agent's authors_regs.do (work dir code/): areg y adoption_shortterm adoption_mediumterm adoption_longterm _Iperiod*, abs(user_id) vce(cluster user_id) on the rebuilt preclean.dta with the authors' sample filters (tables.do line 253); fixest reproduces b and SE (fixef.K = 'full') to < 1e-11 and N exactly

treat_bins: authors' bins in event time (tables.do define_adoption_dummies, cutoffs lines 679-680): short run = weeks 0-1, medium run = 2-24, long run = 25+ since adoption, 1 only for adopters; reference = all pre-adoption weeks of adopters plus all weeks of matched never-adopters; no leads. Recorded in event_structure (Nov 2); the pipeline now estimates these bins directly. event_pre_min/event_post_max are the superseded legacy coding (single-week dummies 0..24 averaged, 25+ endpoint) and are ignored when event_structure is present. Table 8: the long-run bin has no rows (sample ends at week 25) and is not estimated.

notes: EVENT version of Table 8 column 3 (program table_breadth_earlyvslate, tables.do line 387). Outcome: log(unique artists), adopters only, weeks <= median adoption week (25). Table 8 early-vs-late design (lines 387-426): outcome set to missing for matched never-adopters and for weeks after the median adoption week of main-sample users ($adoption_split = 25), so late adopters (adoption week 26-66) are the not-yet-treated controls; 447 adopters, 220 of them never treated inside the window; long-run bin all zero and dropped. The authors' table note says the split is '23 weeks into the main sample'; the median adoption week is 25 in the rebuilt matched sample and also among all 507 kept adopters before matching, so the discrepancy is not caused by the matching step. Main sample (tables.do get_data_mainsample, lines 58-66): period > 4, overlap_min <= period <= overlap_max (common observation window of the matched pair), matched == 1; 896 users = 448 adopters + 448 matched never-adopters (1:1 Mahalanobis matching on the logit propensity index, min_period and max_period; mahapick top-3 then mahaselectunique, seed 12345; 59 of 507 adopters left unmatched). Matched controls carry their partner's adoption week in adopt_period but their adoption dummies are always 0, so gvar g_adopt is NA (never treated) for them. Authors' regression: areg rob_luniq_artist adoption_shortterm adoption_mediumterm adoption_longterm _Iperiod*, abs(user_id) vce(cluster user_id); no controls, no weights. Estimation sample: 8445 user-weeks, 447 users; 447 adopters, of which 3 have no pre-adoption row in the outcome sample (always treated) and 220 no post-adoption row; 19 adoption cohorts (weeks) with both untreated and treated rows; never-treated row share 0.000; treatment absorbing, no switch-offs. Nov 2: the pipeline estimates the authors' two bins (event_structure); the earlier single-week re-binning deviation is removed. data_provenance original: raw Last.fm CSVs shipped in the package (external/spotify_panel.csv, external/spotify_users.csv), rebuilt through the authors' importing_spotify_panel.do, matching.do and preclean.do (work copies with absolute paths; graphs, fitstat and coefplot commented out). Prepared file: mksc1051_mainsample.rds = preclean.dta restricted to the main sample plus g_adopt, adoption bins, adoption_one and the Table 8 rob_ outcomes.

event_structure.source: code/tables.do define_adoption_dummies (lines 284-298; cutoffs $cutoff_shortterm = 1, $cutoff_mediumterm = 24, lines 679-680) and make_regression_table (line 253): areg y adoption_shortterm adoption_mediumterm adoption_longterm _Iperiod*, abs(user_id). Event time periods_since_adoption = period - adopt_period (preclean.do line 65); the dummies are 1 only for adopters with periods_since_adoption in 0-1, 2-24 and 25+; no leads, so every pre-adoption week of an adopter and every week of a matched never-adopter is the reference. Weekly periods 5-66 have no gaps in any outcome sample, every adopter's g_adopt (7-66) is a sample week, so rel = t - g equals periods_since_adoption exactly. Table 8 cols 3-4: the sample ends at week 25 (outcome missing afterwards and for never-adopters), so adoption_longterm is identically zero and omitted by the authors (tables.do line 429); the 25+ bin is not listed here because it has no rows.
event_structure.verified: fixest y ~ i(ebin, ref = 0) | user_id + period (cluster user_id) with es_assign on the run_spec time index reproduces the authors' areg bin coefficients (Stata re-run on the rebuilt matched sample, authors_code) to max abs diff 4.0e-13 (SE 9.0e-14); rel equals the authors' periods_since_adoption on every adopter row and the bins equal the authors' dummies on every row (0 mismatches). N 8445 vs authors 8445. The rebuilt sample equals the published one: N, users and all printed coefficients and SEs agree to printed precision (Nov 2, article PDF). Same sample as the pipeline (no switch-offs, no pre-sample adopters). Script: ~/did_packages/_work/mksc.2017.1051/output/nov2_event_structure_check.csv (scratch verify_1051.R).
